records.literal_gloss: And there was a man from [the] hill country of Ephraim, and his name [was] Micah.

en.L: And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name [was] Micah.
en.B: There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah.
en.R: There was a man named Micah who lived in the hills of Ephraim.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na mtu wa nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Mika.
sw.B: Palikuwa na mtu mmoja wa nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, jina lake Mika.
sw.R: Palikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Mika aliyeishi katika milima ya Efraimu.

es.L: Y había un hombre de la región montañosa de Efraín, y su nombre [era] Micaía.
es.B: Había un hombre de la región montañosa de Efraín que se llamaba Micaía.
es.R: Había un hombre llamado Micaía que vivía en los montes de Efraín.

decisions.choice: Micah: in this verse the longer form of the name, meaning "Who is like Yahweh?"
decisions.reason: In verses 1 and 4 the name has its full form, Micayehu, which means "Who is like Yahweh?"; from verse 5 on it is the short form Micah. The name asks a question the story answers against him: the man who bears it makes an image of silver to stand for the God who forbade images (Exodus 20:4). Both forms name the same man.

decisions.choice: And there was a man: the opening of a new story
decisions.reason: The same words open the story of Manoah in 13:2 and of Elkanah in 1 Samuel 1:1. Here they begin the last part of the book (chapters 17-21), which tells of no judge and no enemy from outside, but of how Israel lived in the time before the kings (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the hills of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Readable says "hills" for the hill country, the high central land given to the tribe of Ephraim (Joshua 17:15).

decisions.choice: "Micaía" throughout chapters 17-18
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for Spanish. The Hebrew gives the longer form of the name here and in verse 4 and the shorter form elsewhere (m1); Spanish uses one form for the one man, so the reader is not led to think of two people.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִמּ֡וֹ אֶלֶף֩ וּמֵאָ֨ה הַכֶּ֜סֶף אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֻֽקַּֽח־לָ֗ךְ וְאַ֤תְּ אָלִית֙ וְגַם֙ אָמַ֣רְתְּ בְּאָזְנַ֔י הִנֵּֽה־הַכֶּ֥סֶף אִתִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י לְקַחְתִּ֑יו וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אִמּ֔וֹ בָּר֥וּךְ בְּנִ֖י לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to his mother, The 1,100 [of] the silver which was taken from you, and you uttered a curse, and also you said [it] in my ears, here! the silver [is] with me; I took it. And said his mother, Blessed [be] my son by Yahweh.

en.L: And he said to his mother, "The 1,100 [shekels of] silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse and also spoke [it] in my ears: look, the silver [is] with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed [be] my son by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: He said to his mother, "You know the {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}} that was taken from you, and how you pronounced a curse over it, and I heard you say it? Look, I have the silver. I am the one who took it." His mother said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless my son!"
en.R: One day Micah said to his mother, "Someone took {{units:about 28 pounds|1,100 shekels}} of silver from you, and I heard you put a curse on the one who did it. Well, I have the silver. I took it." His mother said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, my son!"

sw.L: Naye akamwambia mama yake, "Zile [shekeli] 1,100 za fedha ulizonyang'anywa, ambazo uliapiza laana juu yake, tena ukasema masikioni mwangu: tazama, fedha hiyo [iko] kwangu; mimi niliichukua." Naye mama yake akasema, "Mwanangu [na] abarikiwe na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Alimwambia mama yake, "Unajua zile {{units:karibu kilo 13 za fedha|shekeli 1,100 za fedha}} ulizoibiwa, na jinsi ulivyotamka laana juu yake, nami nikakusikia ukisema? Tazama, fedha hiyo iko kwangu. Ni mimi niliyeichukua." Mama yake akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki, mwanangu!"
sw.R: Siku moja Mika alimwambia mama yake, "Mtu fulani alikuibia {{units:karibu kilo 13|shekeli 1,100}} za fedha, nami nilikusikia ukimlaani yule aliyefanya hivyo. Basi, fedha hiyo iko kwangu. Ni mimi niliyeichukua." Mama yake alisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki, mwanangu!"

es.L: Y dijo a su madre: «Los 1100 [siclos de] plata que te fueron tomados, por los que pronunciaste una maldición y también [la] dijiste a mis oídos: he aquí, la plata [está] conmigo; yo la tomé». Y su madre dijo: «Bendito [sea] mi hijo por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: Le dijo a su madre: «¿Recuerdas los {{units:unos 13 kilos de plata|1100 siclos de plata}} que te robaron, y cómo echaste una maldición sobre ellos, y yo te oí decirla? Pues mira, la plata la tengo yo. Yo fui quien la tomó». Su madre le dijo: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendiga a mi hijo!».
es.R: Un día Micaía le dijo a su madre: «Alguien te robó {{units:unos 13 kilos|1100 siclos}} de plata, y yo te oí maldecir al que lo hizo. Pues bien, la plata la tengo yo. Yo la tomé». Su madre le dijo: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga, hijo mío!».

decisions.choice: you uttered a curse: a solemn curse on the thief, spoken aloud
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a public oath or curse that called on God to punish a wrongdoer who did not come forward (Leviticus 5:1; 1 Kings 8:31). The mother cursed whoever had taken her silver, and her son heard it. The story suggests he confessed because he feared the curse, not because he was sorry.

decisions.choice: Blessed be my son by the LORD: a blessing spoken to cancel the curse
decisions.reason: A spoken curse was thought to go on working, so the mother at once speaks a blessing over her son in the LORD's name to undo it. She does not rebuke him for the theft.

decisions.choice: 1,100 pieces of silver: the same sum each Philistine lord offered Delilah
decisions.reason: In 16:5 each lord of the Philistines promised Delilah 1,100 pieces of silver to betray Samson. The next story opens with the same large sum, now stolen within a family. The silver is not coined money but a weight of silver; the unit, the shekel, is not named but is understood, as often (Genesis 20:16).

decisions.choice: you: an older spelling of the word, read in the usual way
decisions.reason: The consonants of the Hebrew text spell the word for "you" (said to a woman) in an older form, and the scribes' note in the margin reads it in the common form. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: [shekels of] silver
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "1,100 of silver", leaving the unit understood. Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets; Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the shekels as the alternative. A shekel was about two-fifths of an ounce, so 1,100 shekels was about 27 1/2 pounds.

decisions.choice: You know ... and I heard you say it? / Well, I have the silver.
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence starts with the silver, adds what the mother did, then breaks off with "look". Balanced turns the opening into a reminder and Readable into short statements, so that the confession comes at the end, as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "unos 13 kilos" by default, "1100 siclos" with the measures setting
decisions.reason: For chapters 17-21: metric by default where the English converts, the original unit as the alternative, as the Pentateuch terms set (a shekel about 11.5 g, so 1,100 shekels about 12.7 kg, rounded as the English rounds). Literal keeps "siclos" with no setting.

source.text: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־אֶֽלֶף־וּמֵאָ֥ה הַכֶּ֖סֶף לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אִמּ֡וֹ הַקְדֵּ֣שׁ הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף֩ לַיהוָ֨ה מִיָּדִ֜י לִבְנִ֗י לַֽעֲשׂוֹת֙ פֶּ֣סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֔ה וְעַתָּ֖ה אֲשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned the 1,100 [of] the silver to his mother, and said his mother, Surely I consecrate the silver to Yahweh from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image; and now I will return it to you.

en.L: And he returned the 1,100 [shekels of] silver to his mother, and his mother said, "I solemnly consecrate the silver to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast idol; and now I will return it to you."
en.B: When he gave the {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}} back to his mother, she said, "I solemnly dedicate this silver to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from my own hand, for my son, to make a carved image and a cast idol. So now I will give it back to you."
en.R: Micah gave the {{units:28 pounds|1,100 shekels}} of silver back to his mother. Then she said, "I am giving this silver to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I give it for my son, to make a carved idol and an idol of melted metal. So now I will give it back to you."

sw.L: Naye akamrudishia mama yake zile [shekeli] 1,100 za fedha, naye mama yake akasema, "Hakika naiweka wakfu fedha hii kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kutoka mkononi mwangu kwa ajili ya mwanangu, ili kufanya sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu; basi sasa nitakurudishia."
sw.B: Alipomrudishia mama yake zile {{units:karibu kilo 13 za fedha|shekeli 1,100 za fedha}}, alisema, "Naiweka wakfu kabisa fedha hii kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kutoka mkononi mwangu mwenyewe, kwa ajili ya mwanangu, ili kufanya sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu. Kwa hiyo sasa nitakurudishia."
sw.R: Mika alimrudishia mama yake zile {{units:kilo 13|shekeli 1,100}} za fedha. Ndipo alisema, "Ninampa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} fedha hii. Ninaitoa kwa ajili ya mwanangu, ili kutengeneza sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Kwa hiyo sasa nitakurudishia."

es.L: Y devolvió los 1100 [siclos de] plata a su madre, y su madre dijo: «Solemnemente consagro la plata {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de mi mano para mi hijo, para hacer una imagen tallada y un ídolo fundido; y ahora te la devolveré».
es.B: Cuando él le devolvió a su madre los {{units:unos 13 kilos de plata|1100 siclos de plata}}, ella dijo: «Consagro solemnemente esta plata {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, de mi propia mano, para mi hijo, para hacer una imagen tallada y un ídolo fundido. Así que ahora te la devuelvo».
es.R: Micaía le devolvió a su madre los {{units:13 kilos|1100 siclos}} de plata. Entonces ella dijo: «Le doy esta plata {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Se la doy por mi hijo, para hacer un ídolo tallado y un ídolo de metal fundido. Así que ahora te la devuelvo».

decisions.choice: consecrated to the LORD to make an image: worship of the LORD in a form he forbade
decisions.reason: The mother means to honor the LORD; she names him and gives the silver to him. But the very thing she plans is forbidden: "You shall not make for yourself a carved image" (Exodus 20:4). Deuteronomy 27:15 curses the man who makes "a carved image and a cast image", the same pair of words used here. So the family escapes one curse only to do what the law curses.

decisions.choice: a carved image and a cast idol: two objects, or one image made in two ways
alternatives: one image, carved and overlaid with metal
decisions.reason: A carved image (pesel) was shaped from wood or stone, a cast image (massekah) poured from molten metal. Here a silversmith makes them (verse 4). The two may be separate objects, as 18:17-18 lists them separately; or the pair may describe one image, a carved figure overlaid with silver, since 18:20 and 18:30-31 speak of the carved image alone. Either way the text keeps both words.

decisions.choice: I solemnly consecrate: a vow made, or made now, by the mother
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Its form can mean that she had already vowed the silver before it was stolen, or that she vows it now as she receives it back. Either way the silver now belongs to the LORD in her eyes.

decisions.choice: and now I will return it to you: she hands the silver back to her son for the work
alternatives: verse 4 repeats the return of verse 3
Micah gives the silver back again
decisions.reason: Her words seem to give the silver back to Micah so that he can have the image made "for my son". Verse 4 then says he returned it to his mother and she took part of it to the silversmith. Verse 4 may simply take up the story again from the start of verse 3, or Micah may have refused the gift and given the silver back a second time. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: cast idol
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "cast idol" for the poured metal image, so that it is not taken for an ordinary metal object. Readable says "an idol of melted metal".

decisions.choice: "karibu kilo 13" for 1,100 shekels, "karibu kilo 2.3" for 200 (verse 4), "karibu gramu 115" for ten (verse 10), with the shekels as the reader setting
decisions.reason: Metric by default, as for Delilah's silver in 16:5, at 11.5 g a shekel; Literal keeps "shekeli" in brackets, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "sanamu ya kuchonga" (carved image) and "sanamu ya kusubu" (cast idol); Readable "sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa"
decisions.reason: "Kusubu" is to cast metal in a mould; Readable says it in plainer words, as the English Readable does ("an idol of melted metal"). Swahili uses "sanamu" for both, so the two objects stay side by side, as the meaning decision leaves open whether they are one or two.

source.text: וַיָּ֥שֶׁב אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַתִּקַּ֣ח אִמּוֹ֩ מָאתַ֨יִם כֶּ֜סֶף וַתִּתְּנֵ֣הוּ לַצּוֹרֵ֗ף וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ פֶּ֣סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֔ה וַיְהִ֖י בְּבֵ֥ית מִיכָֽיְהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned the silver to his mother, and took his mother 200 [of] silver, and gave it to the silversmith, and he made it [into] a carved image and a cast image; and it was in [the] house of Micah.

en.L: And he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took 200 [shekels of] silver and gave it to the silversmith, and he made it [into] a carved image and a cast idol; and it was in the house of Micah.
en.B: So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took {{units:about 5 pounds of silver|200 shekels of silver}} and gave it to a silversmith. He made it into a carved image and a cast idol, and it was kept in Micah's house.
en.R: So Micah gave the silver back to his mother. She took {{units:about 5 pounds|200 shekels}} of it and gave it to a silversmith. He used it to make a carved idol and an idol of melted metal, and they were put in Micah's house.

sw.L: Naye akamrudishia mama yake ile fedha, naye mama yake akatwaa [shekeli] 200 za fedha, akampa mfua fedha, naye akaifanya [kuwa] sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu; nayo ikawa katika nyumba ya Mika.
sw.B: Basi alimrudishia mama yake ile fedha, naye akachukua {{units:karibu kilo 2.3 za fedha|shekeli 200 za fedha}}, akampa mfua fedha. Naye akaifanya kuwa sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya kusubu, nayo ikawekwa katika nyumba ya Mika.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Mika alimrudishia mama yake ile fedha. Alichukua {{units:karibu kilo 2.3|shekeli 200}} za fedha hiyo, akampa mfua fedha. Mfua fedha aliitumia kutengeneza sanamu ya kuchonga na sanamu ya chuma kilichoyeyushwa, nazo zikawekwa katika nyumba ya Mika.

es.L: Y él devolvió la plata a su madre, y su madre tomó 200 [siclos de] plata y los dio al platero, y él hizo de ella una imagen tallada y un ídolo fundido; y estuvo en la casa de Micaía.
es.B: Así que él le devolvió la plata a su madre, y ella tomó {{units:unos 2,3 kilos de plata|200 siclos de plata}} y se los dio a un platero. Él hizo con ellos una imagen tallada y un ídolo fundido, que quedaron en la casa de Micaía.
es.R: Así que Micaía le devolvió la plata a su madre. Ella tomó {{units:unos 2,3 kilos|200 siclos}} y se los dio a un platero. Con ellos el platero hizo un ídolo tallado y un ídolo de metal fundido, y los pusieron en la casa de Micaía.

decisions.choice: 200 of the silver: only part of what she had dedicated
decisions.reason: She had given all 1,100 pieces to the LORD (verse 3), but she takes 200 to the silversmith. The text does not say what became of the rest.

decisions.choice: it was in the house of Micah: the image or images set up in his home
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, "it was". It may refer to the image as one object (see verse 3) or to the whole work of the silversmith. The point is where it stood: in a private house, not at the place the LORD chose (18:31).

decisions.choice: the silversmith: a craftsman who refined and shaped metal
decisions.reason: The word means one who refines metal by fire. Isaiah 40:19 and 46:6 describe such craftsmen being paid to make gods of silver and gold.

decisions.choice: it was kept / they were put
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the singular "it"; Readable, which spoke of two idols, says "they". The decision in verse 3 leaves open whether there were one or two objects.

source.text: וְהָאִ֣ישׁ מִיכָ֔ה ל֖וֹ בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֵפוֹד֙ וּתְרָפִ֔ים וַיְמַלֵּ֗א אֶת־יַ֤ד אַחַד֙ מִבָּנָ֔יו וַיְהִי־ל֖וֹ לְכֹהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the man Micah, to him [was] a house of God; and he made an ephod and teraphim, and he filled [the] hand of one of his sons, and he became to him a priest.

en.L: And the man Micah had a house of God; and he made an ephod and household gods, and filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became his priest.
en.B: Now this man Micah had a shrine. He made an ephod and household gods, and ordained one of his sons, who became his priest.
en.R: Micah had his own shrine, a house for worshiping God. He made an ephod, a holy object used in worship, and some small household idols. Then he made one of his own sons his priest.

sw.L: Naye mtu huyo Mika alikuwa na nyumba ya Mungu; akafanya efodi na terafimu, akaujaza mkono wa mmoja wa wanawe, naye akawa kuhani wake.
sw.B: Basi mtu huyu Mika alikuwa na mahali pake pa ibada. Alitengeneza efodi na miungu ya nyumbani, akamweka wakfu mmoja wa wanawe, naye akawa kuhani wake.
sw.R: Mika alikuwa na mahali pake mwenyewe pa ibada, nyumba ya kumwabudu Mungu. Alitengeneza efodi, kitu kitakatifu kilichotumika katika ibada, na sanamu ndogo za miungu ya nyumbani. Kisha akamfanya mmoja wa wanawe mwenyewe kuwa kuhani wake.

es.L: Y el hombre Micaía tenía una casa de Dios; e hizo un efod y dioses domésticos, y llenó la mano de uno de sus hijos, y este fue su sacerdote.
es.B: Este hombre, Micaía, tenía un santuario. Hizo un efod y dioses domésticos, y consagró a uno de sus hijos, que llegó a ser su sacerdote.
es.R: Micaía tenía su propio santuario, una casa para adorar a Dios. Hizo un efod, un objeto sagrado que se usaba en el culto, y algunos pequeños ídolos de la casa. Después nombró sacerdote suyo a uno de sus propios hijos.

decisions.choice: a house of God: a private shrine
decisions.reason: The words can mean "a house of God" or "a house of gods", since the same Hebrew word serves for both. Micah thinks he is serving the LORD (verse 13), so "God" fits his intention, while the images and household gods inside show what it became. The phrase is the same as the name Bethel, "house of God", where Israel did have a place of worship (20:18, 26), but this is one man's house.

decisions.choice: an ephod: an object used at a shrine to seek answers from God
decisions.reason: In Exodus 28:6-14 the ephod is part of the high priest's dress, worn with the breastpiece through which God's will was asked. Here, as with Gideon's ephod (8:27), it is an object kept at a shrine. In 18:5 Micah's priest is asked to inquire of God, probably by means of it.

decisions.choice: teraphim: household gods
decisions.reason: The teraphim were figures of gods kept in a home, perhaps to protect it or to give guidance (Genesis 31:19, 34; 1 Samuel 19:13; Ezekiel 21:26). Josiah later removed them as forbidden (2 Kings 23:24).

decisions.choice: filled the hand of: installed as priest
decisions.reason: To "fill the hand" is the phrase for ordaining a priest (Exodus 28:41; 29:9). The law gave the priesthood to Aaron's descendants (Numbers 3:10), but Micah, from the tribe of Ephraim, makes his own son priest.

decisions.choice: a shrine; household gods / small household idols
decisions.reason: Balanced says "shrine" for a private place of worship, keeping the question of "God" or "gods" in the meaning decision. Readable adds "a house for worshiping God" and explains the ephod and teraphim briefly, as 8:27 and Genesis 31:19 do.

decisions.choice: ordained
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the word English uses for making someone a priest, as in Exodus 29:9; Literal keeps "filled the hand".

decisions.choice: "terafimu" at Literal, "miungu ya nyumbani" (household gods) at Balanced and Readable; "akaujaza mkono wa" (filled the hand of) at Literal, "akamweka wakfu" (consecrated) at Balanced
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word and idiom so the reader can see them; Balanced and Readable say what they mean (m3, m4), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "llenó la mano de" (L); "consagró" (B); "nombró sacerdote" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom for installing a priest (m4); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: In the days the those there [was] no king in Israel; each the right in his eyes he did.

en.L: In those days [there was] no king in Israel; each did what [was] right in his own eyes.
en.B: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what they thought was right.
en.R: At that time Israel had no king. Everyone did whatever seemed right to them.

sw.L: Katika siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli; kila mtu alifanya yaliyo sawa machoni pake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Siku hizo hapakuwa na mfalme katika Israeli; kila mtu alifanya alivyoona ni sawa.
sw.R: Wakati huo Israeli hawakuwa na mfalme. Kila mtu alifanya lolote alilodhani ni sawa.

es.L: En aquellos días no [había] rey en Israel; cada uno hacía lo recto a sus propios ojos.
es.B: En aquellos días no había rey en Israel; cada uno hacía lo que le parecía bien.
es.R: En aquel tiempo Israel no tenía rey. Cada uno hacía lo que le parecía bien.

decisions.choice: each did what was right in his own eyes: each person was his own standard
decisions.reason: Israel was to do "what is right in the eyes of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 12:25, 28; 13:19), and Moses warned against each one doing "whatever is right in his own eyes" (Deuteronomy 12:8). Micah's shrine is an example: he means well and is sure the LORD will bless him (verse 13), but he follows his own judgment, not God's law.

decisions.choice: there was no king in Israel: a refrain of the last chapters
decisions.reason: The words come back in 18:1 and 19:1, and the whole saying again at the very end of the book (21:25). They look back from a later time when Israel had kings, and they show the disorder of the time. The book does not say whether a human king would solve the problem; Gideon had said that the LORD was Israel's ruler (8:23).

decisions.choice: everyone did what they thought was right
decisions.reason: "In his own eyes" means by one's own judgment. Balanced and Readable say so plainly, and use "everyone ... they", since the saying covers all the people. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: "kila mtu alifanya alivyoona ni sawa" (everyone did as he saw was right) at Balanced; Literal keeps "machoni pake mwenyewe" (in his own eyes)
decisions.reason: The refrain of 17:6 and 21:25, worded as agreed for every language: "kila mtu" is already inclusive, so Swahili needs no gender wording, and both places read alike.

decisions.choice: "cada uno hacía lo recto a sus propios ojos" (L); "cada uno hacía lo que le parecía bien" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for the refrain of 17:6 and 21:25. Spanish "cada uno" already takes in everyone, man or woman, so there is no gender setting.

source.text: וַיְהִי־נַ֗עַר מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֨חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִמִּשְׁפַּ֖חַת יְהוּדָ֑ה וְה֥וּא לֵוִ֖י וְה֥וּא גָֽר־שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And there was a young man from Bethlehem [of] Judah, from [the] clan of Judah, and he [was] a Levite, and he [was] sojourning there.

en.L: And there was a young man from Bethlehem [of] Judah, from the clan of Judah, and he [was] a Levite, and he [was] sojourning there.
en.B: There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah. He was a Levite and had been living there as an outsider.
en.R: There was also a young man from the town of Bethlehem in Judah. He belonged to a family in the tribe of Judah, but he was a Levite. He had been living there for a while.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na kijana kutoka Bethlehemu [ya] Yuda, wa ukoo wa Yuda, naye [alikuwa] Mlawi, naye [alikuwa] akikaa huko kama mgeni.
sw.B: Palikuwa na kijana mmoja kutoka Bethlehemu ya Yuda, wa ukoo wa Yuda. Alikuwa Mlawi, naye alikuwa akiishi huko kama mgeni.
sw.R: Palikuwa pia na kijana mmoja kutoka mji wa Bethlehemu katika Yuda. Alikuwa wa jamaa moja katika kabila la Yuda, lakini alikuwa Mlawi. Alikuwa ameishi huko kwa muda.

es.L: Y había un joven de Belén de Judá, del clan de Judá, y él [era] levita, y residía allí como forastero.
es.B: Había un joven de Belén de Judá, del clan de Judá. Era levita y había vivido allí como forastero.
es.R: También había un joven del pueblo de Belén, en Judá. Pertenecía a una familia de la tribu de Judá, pero era levita. Había estado viviendo allí por un tiempo.

decisions.choice: of the clan of Judah, and a Levite: a Levite who had lived among the people of Judah
alternatives: a man of Judah who served as a Levite
decisions.reason: Levites had no land of their own and lived in towns among the other tribes (Numbers 35:2-8; Joshua 21). Bethlehem was not one of the Levite towns. "From the clan of Judah" probably means he had been counted with the people of Judah where he lived, not that his father was from Judah. 18:30 names him as a descendant of Moses through Gershom.

decisions.choice: sojourning there: living as a resident from elsewhere
decisions.reason: The verb describes a person who lives in a place without belonging to it by family or land, as Levites did (Deuteronomy 18:6). The words "sojourner there" sound like the name Gershom, his ancestor (18:30; Exodus 2:22).

decisions.choice: living there as an outsider
decisions.reason: Balanced says "outsider", as it does for the related noun (Leviticus 19:34), since the man was at home neither by land nor by family.

decisions.choice: He belonged to a family in the tribe of Judah, but he was a Levite.
decisions.reason: Readable adds "but" to show that a Levite and a man of the clan of Judah would not normally be the same; the meaning decision explains the link.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הָאִ֜ישׁ מֵהָעִ֗יר מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֨חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה לָג֖וּר בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִמְצָ֑א וַיָּבֹ֧א הַר־אֶפְרַ֛יִם עַד־בֵּ֥ית מִיכָ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the man from the city, from Bethlehem [of] Judah, to sojourn where he would find; and he came [to the] hill country of Ephraim, to [the] house of Micah, to make his way.

en.L: And the man went from the city, from Bethlehem [of] Judah, to sojourn wherever he might find [a place]; and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he made his way.
en.B: The man left the town of Bethlehem in Judah to find somewhere else to live. As he traveled, he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to Micah's house.
en.R: This man left Bethlehem in Judah to look for another place to live. On his way he came to the hills of Ephraim, to Micah's house.

sw.L: Naye mtu huyo akaondoka katika mji, kutoka Bethlehemu [ya] Yuda, ili akae kama mgeni popote atakapopata [mahali]; akafika katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, kwenye nyumba ya Mika, alipokuwa akienda njia yake.
sw.B: Mtu huyo aliondoka katika mji wa Bethlehemu ya Yuda ili kutafuta mahali pengine pa kuishi. Alipokuwa akisafiri, alifika katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, kwenye nyumba ya Mika.
sw.R: Mtu huyo aliondoka Bethlehemu ya Yuda kutafuta mahali pengine pa kuishi. Njiani alifika katika milima ya Efraimu, kwenye nyumba ya Mika.

es.L: Y el hombre se fue de la ciudad, de Belén de Judá, para residir donde hallara [lugar]; y llegó a la región montañosa de Efraín, a la casa de Micaía, mientras seguía su camino.
es.B: Aquel hombre dejó la ciudad de Belén de Judá para buscar otro lugar donde vivir. En su viaje llegó a la región montañosa de Efraín, a la casa de Micaía.
es.R: Este hombre se fue de Belén de Judá para buscar otro lugar donde vivir. En el camino llegó a los montes de Efraín, a la casa de Micaía.

decisions.choice: wherever he might find: he had no fixed place in mind
decisions.reason: The clause has no object. He goes to settle wherever he can find a place, and perhaps a living; the following verses show him taking the first good offer.

decisions.choice: to make his way: as he traveled
decisions.reason: The phrase means going along one's road. He came to Micah's house on the way, not because he was looking for it.

decisions.choice: [a place]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object the Hebrew leaves understood.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר־ל֥וֹ מִיכָ֖ה מֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו לֵוִ֣י אָנֹ֗כִי מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֨חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאָנֹכִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ לָג֖וּר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶמְצָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Micah, From where do you come? And he said to him, A Levite I [am] from Bethlehem [of] Judah, and I [am] going to sojourn where I will find.

en.L: And Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I [am] a Levite from Bethlehem [of] Judah, and I [am] going to sojourn wherever I may find [a place]."
en.B: Micah asked him, "Where have you come from?" He answered, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to settle wherever I can find a place."
en.R: Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah. I am looking for a place to live."

sw.L: Naye Mika akamwambia, "Unatoka wapi?" Naye akamwambia, "Mimi [ni] Mlawi kutoka Bethlehemu [ya] Yuda, nami ninakwenda kukaa kama mgeni popote nitakapopata [mahali]."
sw.B: Mika alimwuliza, "Umetoka wapi?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni Mlawi kutoka Bethlehemu ya Yuda, nami ninakwenda kuishi popote nitakapopata mahali."
sw.R: Mika alimwuliza, "Wewe ni wa wapi?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni Mlawi kutoka Bethlehemu ya Yuda. Ninatafuta mahali pa kuishi."

es.L: Y Micaía le dijo: «¿De dónde vienes?». Y él le dijo: «Levita [soy], de Belén de Judá, y voy a residir donde halle [lugar]».
es.B: Micaía le preguntó: «¿De dónde vienes?». Él respondió: «Soy levita, de Belén de Judá, y voy a establecerme donde encuentre lugar».
es.R: Micaía le preguntó: «¿De dónde eres?». Él contestó: «Soy levita, de Belén de Judá. Estoy buscando un lugar donde vivir».

decisions.choice: A Levite I am: the word he puts first
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the young man's answer begins with "Levite". It is the thing that makes him worth hiring, and Micah seizes on it at once (verses 10 and 13).

decisions.choice: settle / a place to live
decisions.reason: "Sojourn" here means living for a time where one does not belong (verse 7). Balanced says "settle" and Readable "a place to live".

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ מִיכָ֜ה שְׁבָ֣ה עִמָּדִ֗י וֶֽהְיֵה־לִי֮ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵן֒ וְאָנֹכִ֨י אֶֽתֶּן־לְךָ֜ עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת כֶּ֨סֶף֙ לַיָּמִ֔ים וְעֵ֥רֶךְ בְּגָדִ֖ים וּמִחְיָתֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הַלֵּוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Micah, Stay with me and be to me for a father and for a priest, and I will give to you ten [of] silver for the days, and a set of garments, and your food. And went the Levite.

en.L: And Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten [shekels of] silver a year, and a set of garments, and your food." And the Levite went.
en.B: Then Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me. I will give you {{units:about 4 ounces of silver|ten shekels of silver}} a year, a set of clothes, and your food." So the Levite went in.
en.R: Then Micah said, "Stay here with me. Be my adviser and my priest. Each year I will pay you {{units:about 4 ounces|ten shekels}} of silver. I will also give you clothes and food." So the Levite went in.

sw.L: Naye Mika akamwambia, "Kaa kwangu, uwe kwangu baba na kuhani, nami nitakupa [shekeli] kumi za fedha kwa mwaka, na jozi ya mavazi, na chakula chako." Naye yule Mlawi akaenda.
sw.B: Kisha Mika alimwambia, "Kaa kwangu, uwe baba na kuhani kwangu. Nitakupa {{units:karibu gramu 115 za fedha|shekeli kumi za fedha}} kwa mwaka, jozi ya mavazi, na chakula chako." Basi yule Mlawi akaingia.
sw.R: Kisha Mika alisema, "Kaa hapa kwangu. Uwe mshauri wangu na kuhani wangu. Kila mwaka nitakulipa {{units:karibu gramu 115|shekeli kumi}} za fedha. Nitakupa pia mavazi na chakula." Basi yule Mlawi akaingia.

es.L: Y Micaía le dijo: «Quédate conmigo, y sé para mí padre y sacerdote, y yo te daré diez [siclos de] plata al año, y un juego de vestidos, y tu comida». Y el levita entró.
es.B: Entonces Micaía le dijo: «Quédate conmigo y sé para mí padre y sacerdote. Te daré {{units:unos 115 gramos de plata|diez siclos de plata}} al año, ropa y comida». Y el levita entró.
es.R: Entonces Micaía le dijo: «Quédate aquí conmigo. Sé mi consejero y mi sacerdote. Cada año te pagaré {{units:unos 115 gramos|diez siclos}} de plata. También te daré ropa y comida». Y el levita entró.

decisions.choice: a father: a title of honor for a priest or adviser
decisions.reason: "Father" was a title for a respected priest, prophet or counselor (18:19; 2 Kings 6:21; Genesis 45:8). Micah gives the title to a young man, who in the next verse becomes "like one of his sons".

decisions.choice: for the days: each year
decisions.reason: "The days" here means a full year, as in 1 Samuel 1:21 and 2:19, where "the yearly sacrifice" uses the same word. Ten shekels a year, with clothes and food, was a modest living.

decisions.choice: and the Levite went: the sense is not clear
decisions.reason: The two words come at the end of Micah's offer. They may mean the Levite went into Micah's house, or went along with the offer; or they may anticipate the next verse. Some think they arose from a copying slip, since verse 11 begins with a similar-looking verb, "he agreed".

decisions.choice: my adviser
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the title "father" (m1) rather than the word, which a reader might take literally.

decisions.choice: went in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "went in", the simplest sense of the verb after an invitation to stay; the decision m3 notes the uncertainty.

source.text: וַיּ֥וֹאֶל הַלֵּוִ֖י לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אֶת־הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיְהִ֤י הַנַּ֨עַר֙ ל֔וֹ כְּאַחַ֖ד מִבָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And agreed the Levite to stay with the man, and became the young man to him like one of his sons.

en.L: And the Levite agreed to stay with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
en.B: The Levite agreed to stay with the man, and the young man became like one of his own sons to him.
en.R: The Levite agreed to live with Micah, and Micah treated the young man like one of his own sons.

sw.L: Naye yule Mlawi akakubali kukaa na mtu huyo, naye yule kijana akawa kwake kama mmoja wa wanawe.
sw.B: Mlawi huyo alikubali kukaa na mtu huyo, naye yule kijana akawa kwake kama mmoja wa wanawe mwenyewe.
sw.R: Mlawi huyo alikubali kuishi na Mika, naye Mika akamtendea yule kijana kama mmoja wa wanawe mwenyewe.

es.L: Y el levita aceptó quedarse con el hombre, y el joven fue para él como uno de sus hijos.
es.B: El levita aceptó quedarse con aquel hombre, y el joven llegó a ser para él como uno de sus propios hijos.
es.R: El levita aceptó vivir con Micaía, y Micaía trató al joven como a uno de sus propios hijos.

decisions.choice: agreed: was willing, consented
decisions.reason: The verb means to be willing or to make up one's mind to do something. The Levite accepts the terms of verse 10.

decisions.choice: like one of his sons: a place in the family, and in the priesthood
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls verse 5, where Micah made "one of his sons" priest. The young man now has that place. He was asked to be a "father" (verse 10) and is treated as a son.

decisions.choice: Micah treated the young man like
decisions.reason: Readable names Micah for "the man" and turns "became to him" into what Micah did, for clarity.

source.text: וַיְמַלֵּ֤א מִיכָה֙ אֶת־יַ֣ד הַלֵּוִ֔י וַיְהִי־ל֥וֹ הַנַּ֖עַר לְכֹהֵ֑ן וַיְהִ֖י בְּבֵ֥ית מִיכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And filled Micah [the] hand of the Levite, and became to him the young man for a priest, and he was in [the] house of Micah.

en.L: And Micah filled the hand of the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and he was in the house of Micah.
en.B: So Micah ordained the Levite. The young man became his priest, living in Micah's household.
en.R: Micah made the Levite a priest. So the young man became Micah's priest and lived in his house.

sw.L: Naye Mika akaujaza mkono wa yule Mlawi, naye yule kijana akawa kuhani wake, akawa katika nyumba ya Mika.
sw.B: Basi Mika alimweka wakfu yule Mlawi. Kijana huyo akawa kuhani wake, akiishi katika nyumba ya Mika.
sw.R: Mika alimfanya yule Mlawi kuwa kuhani. Kwa hiyo kijana huyo akawa kuhani wa Mika, akaishi nyumbani mwake.

es.L: Y Micaía llenó la mano del levita, y el joven fue su sacerdote, y estuvo en la casa de Micaía.
es.B: Así que Micaía consagró al levita. El joven llegó a ser su sacerdote y vivía en la casa de Micaía.
es.R: Micaía nombró sacerdote al levita. Así el joven llegó a ser el sacerdote de Micaía y vivía en su casa.

decisions.choice: filled the hand of the Levite: installed him as priest
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the phrase means ordaining a priest. A Levite who was not a descendant of Aaron could serve at the sanctuary but not as priest (Numbers 3:10; 18:1-7), and Micah has no right to ordain anyone. Yet his shrine now has a priest from the priestly tribe.

decisions.choice: he was in the house of Micah: he lived there
decisions.reason: The words can mean both that he lived in Micah's household and that he served at the shrine in his house (verse 5). The same phrase in verse 4 described where the image stood.

decisions.choice: ordained
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔ה עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּֽי־יֵיטִ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה לִ֑י כִּ֧י הָיָה־לִ֛י הַלֵּוִ֖י לְכֹהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Micah, Now I know that will do good Yahweh to me, for has become to me the Levite for a priest.

en.L: And Micah said, "Now I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do good to me, for the Levite has become my priest."
en.B: Then Micah said, "Now I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will treat me well, because I have a Levite as my priest."
en.R: Then Micah said, "Now I am sure that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bless me, because I have a Levite to be my priest."

sw.L: Naye Mika akasema, "Sasa najua ya kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atanitendea mema, kwa maana Mlawi amekuwa kuhani wangu."
sw.B: Kisha Mika alisema, "Sasa najua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atanitendea mema, kwa sababu nina Mlawi kuwa kuhani wangu."
sw.R: Kisha Mika alisema, "Sasa nina hakika kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atanibariki, kwa sababu nina Mlawi kuwa kuhani wangu."

es.L: Y dijo Micaía: «Ahora sé que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me hará bien, porque el levita ha llegado a ser mi sacerdote».
es.B: Entonces Micaía dijo: «Ahora sé que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me tratará bien, porque tengo un levita como sacerdote».
es.R: Entonces Micaía dijo: «Ahora estoy seguro de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me bendecirá, porque tengo a un levita como sacerdote».

decisions.choice: Now I know that the LORD will do good to me: confidence built on the wrong things
decisions.reason: Micah is sure of the LORD's favor because his shrine has a Levite. But the shrine holds images the LORD forbade (verse 3), the priest is not of Aaron's family, and the place is not the one the LORD chose (Deuteronomy 12:5-14). The next chapter shows how little his arrangements are worth: the Danites take both the images and the priest (18:14-26).

decisions.choice: the Levite: the man who has just been named
decisions.reason: The article points back to the young man of verses 7-12. Micah's reason is that he has a man of the priestly tribe, not only a member of his own family (verse 5).

decisions.choice: I have a Levite as my priest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the Levite has become to me as priest". Balanced and Readable make Micah the subject, which keeps his point: what he has gained.
